chapters.title: Your Affiliate Army
chapters.subtitle: How to get other people to sell your products, honestly, and still keep enough money
chapters.mentor_intro: I'll start with how unknown products usually grow in Brazil. Often the creator is not the one doing most of the selling. Many people sell the same product at the same time, each one to their own audience. Those people are affiliates (afiliados). You are faceless. You have one laptop and a small budget. You cannot be inside 50 teacher groups, 30 couples' pages and 20 church communities at once. Twenty good affiliates can. And you only pay them when a sale happens. In this chapter I show you how to set a commission that is fair to them and still leaves money for you. You will learn what affiliates need before they say yes, where to find them and what to send them. I also show you how to protect your brand. One affiliate who promises miracles can damage your name faster than any competitor. We start small, with 10 honest, well-equipped partners for the Caderno do Casal. Then we grow.
learning_goals: Calculate what you keep per sale when you pay 50% commission on the front product.
Build a complete affiliate kit for Family 1: captions, WhatsApp texts, story scripts, images and rules.
Find the right affiliates and invite them with personal messages that are not spam.
Run simple onboarding, a weekly update and honest contests.
Protect your brand with clear rules, and remove affiliates who break them.

sections.heading: Why affiliates make unknown products explode

blocks.text: In Brazil, selling through affiliates is a normal way to sell digital products. An **affiliate (afiliado)** promotes your product with a personal link. They earn a **commission (comissão)** on every sale that comes from that link. On Hotmart, producers set commissions from 30% to 80%. On Kiwify the range is 40% to 70%. So Brazilian affiliates already know how this works. Many of them look for new products to promote every week.

Why does this matter to you? At the start, your reach is small. One faceless account with 300 followers cannot make 'sales every minute'. But 20 affiliates can, each with their own audience of teachers, couples or church members. They multiply your reach and you pay nothing upfront. You only pay when someone buys. Later in this book you will see that ads cost money even when nobody buys. Affiliates don't.

blocks.title: What a good affiliate gives you
items: **Reach you don't own:** their followers, their groups, their channels.
**Trust:** their audience already knows them, so a recommendation lands softer than an ad.
**Content you didn't make:** they post, film and write in their own style.
**Zero risk upfront:** you pay commission only after a real sale.

blocks.text: An affiliate army is an amplifier. It is not a way around a weak product. If your page doesn't convert when you send it traffic, an affiliate will try once, see zero sales and leave for good. That's why we built the page, the bumps and the organic proof first. Bring in affiliates when you already have a few organic sales, so you can honestly say 'this page sells'.

sections.heading: Commission design: the maths of what you keep

blocks.text: Our plan is **50% commission on the front products** (the R$27 products). For low-ticket products, the research recommends 40-60%. That makes 50% a fair middle: good enough to get attention, and still room for you. Bumps and upsells are where your extra margin lives. So, at the start, keep them 100% yours if your platform lets you choose.

blocks.title: Example: one order, with and without an affiliate (Hotmart Brazil fees, fictional mix)
How I got these numbers (example only)
blocks.text: Start with the average order value (AOV, valor médio do pedido) from your playbook. Every order has the R$27 front. 30% of buyers take the R$12,90 bump, which adds R$3,87 per order on average. 8% take the R$27 upsell, which adds R$2,16. That's about **R$33,10 per order** before fees. Hotmart Brazil charges 9.9% + R$2,49. If the fixed R$2,49 is charged once per order (check this), the fee is about R$5,77. On your own sale you keep about R$27,33. On an affiliate sale you keep about R$13,76. Half can feel painful. But this is a sale you would never have had, and it cost you zero in ads.

Check three things on your platform **before** you invite anyone: (1) Is the commission calculated on the full price or after fees? (2) Can you turn commission off for bumps and upsells? (3) When and how are affiliates paid? EscalePay says it has affiliate features, but that is the company's own claim. Test it with a dummy affiliate account first. If a 50% commission turns out to be calculated in a way you didn't expect, your margin can vanish.
Don't start at 80% to look generous. You can raise the commission later for your best affiliates. Lowering it later breaks trust. Start at 50% on the front product and keep that promise.

sections.heading: What affiliates need before they say yes

blocks.title: The five things good affiliates check
items: **A good page:** clear, fast on mobile, honest, made in Lovable with your real product pages shown.
**High conversion (conversão):** proof that visitors buy. Your organic sales are that proof. Share real numbers only.
**Ready materials:** captions, WhatsApp texts, story scripts and images they can post today.
**Quick support:** answers within 24 hours when they have a question or a buyer has a problem.
**An honest product:** something they are not ashamed to recommend to their own audience.

blocks.title: Build the Family 1 affiliate kit (one Google Drive folder)
items: Create a folder called 'Kit Afiliados - Caderno do Casal' with subfolders: Legendas, WhatsApp, Stories, Imagens, Regras.
Ask Claude for 20 swipe captions (legendas prontas) in PT-BR. Pick the best 10 and check every word yourself.
Write 5 WhatsApp texts: a short one, a story-style one, a gift angle, a 'one date per week' angle, and a reminder.
Write 3 story scripts of 3-4 frames each: hook, inside pages, price and link.
Make 6 images: art from Gemini **without text**, then add the title and price in Canva so the Portuguese accents are correct.
Add a one-page rules document (you will see it at the end of this chapter) and a product summary with price, link and what's inside.

blocks.text: Treat the kit as a product. Name the files clearly ('legenda-01-presente.txt', 'story-02-encontros.png'). A tired affiliate at 10 p.m. should find what they need in 10 seconds.

sections.heading: Where to find affiliates and how to invite them

blocks.title: Where to look
items: **Hotmart marketplace:** list your product with affiliation open, so affiliates searching the marketplace can find it.
**Niche TikTok creators:** search 'encontro de casal', 'devocional casal', 'planner financeiro', 'atividades de Natal escola'. Look for small, active accounts.
**Couple, church and teacher pages** on Instagram and TikTok. These are your core audiences.
**Facebook and WhatsApp groups**, only where the rules allow promotions. Ask the admin first.

blocks.title: Personalised vs generic (example)
blocks.text: Generic: 'Oi, quer ser meu afiliado?' This gets ignored. Personal: you open @casaljuntoscomdeus (fictional page), see a post about 'tempo de qualidade no casamento', and write about that exact post. One real detail shows you actually looked. It takes 2 extra minutes and makes a reply far more likely.

blocks.title: Convite para afiliados (WhatsApp ou direct)
blocks.text: Oi, [nome]! Tudo bem? Acompanho o seu perfil [@perfil] e gostei muito do post sobre [detalhe específico do conteúdo]. Eu criei o 'Caderno do Casal: 52 Encontros para Reconectar', um caderno digital com 52 ideias de encontros para fazer a dois, por R$27. Estou montando um time pequeno de afiliados e lembrei de você, porque o seu público [motivo, ex.: fala muito de casamento e tempo de qualidade]. A comissão é de 50% no produto principal, e eu entrego tudo pronto: legendas, textos para WhatsApp, roteiros de stories e imagens. Posso te mandar o link da página para você dar uma olhada? Se não fizer sentido para o seu público, tudo bem também. Obrigado pela atenção!

Never mass-send invitations. Don't drop your link into groups that don't allow it, and don't send the same message to 200 people. That is spam. It can get your WhatsApp or Instagram blocked and it damages your brand. Send one follow-up after 48 hours at most. If they say no, thank them and move on.

sections.heading: Onboarding and the weekly update

blocks.title: Onboarding a new affiliate (10 minutes each)
items: Approve them on the platform and check their affiliate link opens the right page.
Send a welcome message with the kit folder link, the rules and the product summary.
Suggest one simple first action: 'post story-01 and caption-03 this week'.
Add them to a broadcast list or Telegram channel just for affiliates, so updates reach everyone at once.
Write their name, niche and start date in your affiliate sheet.

blocks.title: Atualização semanal para afiliados
blocks.text: Oi, time! Atualização da semana do Caderno do Casal: 1) O que mais funcionou: vídeos folheando o caderno, com a ideia do encontro escrita na tela. 2) Novidade no kit: 5 legendas novas com o tema 'presente de Natal para o casal'. Já estão na pasta. 3) Teste da semana: postem em horários diferentes e me contem qual funcionou melhor, que eu compartilho com todo mundo. 4) Lembrete: nada de prometer resultado no relacionamento e nada de mandar link em grupo sem permissão do administrador. Qualquer dúvida, me chama aqui. Respondo em até 24 horas. Boas vendas!

Every update needs one real lesson, one new piece of material and one reminder of the rules. Keep it short. Affiliates promote many products. The producer who makes their life easy gets their best effort.

sections.heading: Contests, leaderboards and protecting your brand

blocks.text: A **contest (concurso)** with a **leaderboard (ranking)** can wake up quiet affiliates. Keep it honest. Use real numbers from the platform, set a clear end date, and offer prizes you can actually deliver. Good prizes that cost you no cash: free access to the Mega Kit 2027, a custom set of captions written for their audience, or a feature in your channel. Before you announce any cash prize, check how you can send money from Mozambique to a Brazilian affiliate. A prize you cannot pay destroys trust.

blocks.title: Regras do time de afiliados
blocks.text: Regras do time (leia antes de divulgar): 1) Não prometa resultados: nada de 'vai salvar o seu casamento' ou 'garantido'. 2) Não faça spam: só divulgue em grupos onde o administrador permite. 3) Não invente depoimentos, prints de vendas, avaliações ou rankings. 4) Não crie urgência falsa, como 'últimas unidades' ou 'só hoje', se não for verdade. 5) Se usar pessoas ou cenas realistas feitas com IA, coloque a etiqueta de IA da plataforma. 6) Ficou em dúvida sobre um texto? Me manda antes de postar. Quem quebrar estas regras sai do programa. Obrigado por proteger a marca junto comigo!

Remove an affiliate **immediately** for fake testimonials, promises about money or health, spam, or misleading ads using your brand. For a small mistake, like a caption that is too strong, send one private message with the fix. Before you ever need it, check how your platform blocks an affiliate and what happens to their pending commissions.
Your affiliates speak with your voice. Only recruit people you would be proud to be quoted by.

key_takeaways: Affiliates multiply your reach and you pay only when a sale happens, but they only stay if your page already converts.
50% on the R$27 front product is fair. Keep bumps and upsells as your margin and check how your platform calculates commission.
A ready-to-post kit and replies within 24 hours matter more to affiliates than a big promise.
Personal invitations with one real detail beat mass messages. Spam hurts your brand and your accounts.
Clear rules (no income or result promises, no spam, no fake reviews) protect everyone. Remove affiliates who break them.

challenge.title: Recruit 10
challenge.mission: Prepare the Family 1 affiliate kit, send 30 personalised invitations, sign up 10 affiliates and send them the kit.
steps: Turn on affiliation for 'Caderno do Casal' at 50% on the front product, then test an affiliate link yourself to confirm the right page and checkout open.
Build the kit in one shared Google Drive folder: 10 captions, 5 WhatsApp texts, 3 story scripts, 6 images (Gemini art + Canva titles) and the rules document.
List 40 candidates in Google Sheets (name, profile link, niche, why they fit) from the Hotmart marketplace, TikTok search and couple, church and teacher pages.
Send 30 personalised invitations using the script, each with one real detail from their content. Send one follow-up after 48 hours, never more.
Approve 10 affiliates and send each one the welcome message, the kit link and the rules.
Log every invitation, reply and sign-up in your sheet.
challenge.proof: A screenshot of your platform's affiliate list with 10 approved affiliates, plus your sheet showing 30 invitations sent.
challenge.bonus: Get your first affiliate sale. Then send that affiliate a personal thank-you, ask what worked, and share the lesson with the whole team in your weekly update.

quiz.question: You pay 50% commission on the R$27 front product, calculated on the full price. How much does the affiliate earn per front sale?
quiz.explanation: 50% of R$27 is R$13,50. Always check whether your platform calculates commission on the full price or after fees.

quiz.question: Which affiliate behaviour is a reason for immediate removal?
options: Asking you many questions
Posting a fake buyer testimonial
Making only one sale in a month
Writing their own caption that follows the rules
quiz.explanation: Fake testimonials mislead buyers and break your brand rules. Few sales or lots of questions are normal and fixable.

quiz.question: What makes a recruiting message work best?
options: Sending the same text to 200 groups
Promising they will earn a lot
Mentioning one real detail from their content and offering a ready kit
Asking them to buy the product first
quiz.explanation: Personalisation shows respect, and a ready kit makes saying yes easy. Income promises and mass messages break the rules.

glossary.meaning: A person who promotes your product with a personal link and earns a commission on each sale from it.
The share of the sale price that goes to the affiliate.
Ready-made captions, texts, scripts and images that affiliates can post.
A personal link that tells the platform which affiliate made the sale.
A list of affiliates ordered by real sales, used in contests.

chapters.title: Paid Traffic Without Burning Money
chapters.subtitle: Small Meta Ads tests, clear numbers and strict rules, only after organic sales
chapters.mentor_intro: Paid ads (anúncios pagos) are a megaphone. They make a message louder. They don't make a bad message good. If your page doesn't sell when people arrive from organic content, ads will only help you lose money faster. So this chapter follows one rule above all: no ads until Family 1 has organic sales. Once you have that green light, I take you step by step through Meta Ads from zero: the Business Manager, the Pixel, a Sales campaign, a small budget and the right audience in Brazil. Then we run a careful test at R$20-30 per day, per product, for 5 to 7 days, using creatives taken from your best organic posts. I teach you to read the numbers like a business owner, not a gambler, and to follow simple rules for when to kill, keep or scale an ad. We also cover ad policies, Brazil's ad taxes and how to protect your cash. Small tests and clear rules. And never with borrowed money.
learning_goals: Decide when you are ready for ads using a simple green-light checklist.
Set up Business Manager, the Pixel and a Sales campaign aimed at adults in Brazil.
Plan a 5-7 day test at R$20-30/day using 3-5 creatives from your organic winners.
Read CTR, CPC, cost per checkout, cost per purchase and ROAS, and compare them with your AOV.
Apply kill/keep/scale rules while respecting ad policies, taxes and a daily cash limit.

sections.heading: The green light: when to start ads

blocks.text: Ads are the **last** step of the traffic plan, not the first. Organic content and affiliates show you what works for free. Ads take something that already works and give it more reach. If you start ads too early, you pay Meta to discover what TikTok and Pinterest could have taught you for free.

blocks.title: Green-light checklist (all must be yes)
items: Family 1 has real organic sales from strangers, not from friends.
You made a real test purchase by Pix from a Brazilian buyer and one by card, and delivery worked.
Your refund process works and you honour the 7-day withdrawal right (CDC art. 49).
You know your AOV (example: R$33,10) and your fees.
The test money comes from profit or savings you can afford to lose.

blocks.text: If you have zero organic sales, don't 'test the market' with ads. Fix the page, the offer or the content first. Ads multiply what already exists. Zero multiplied by anything is still zero, and you still pay the ad bill. Also skip TikTok Ads for now: the minimum campaign budget of about USD 50/day is too high for your stage.

sections.heading: Meta Ads from zero: the setup

blocks.title: Set up once, carefully
items: Create a **Business Manager** (gerenciador de negócios), Meta's business account. Menus and names change often, so in Meta it may appear as 'Business portfolio' or 'Meta Business Suite' (check this).

Create a faceless brand Facebook Page and connect your brand Instagram. Meta normally needs a personal profile behind the business account. It is not shown on your ads, but check Meta's current help pages.
Create an **ad account** (conta de anúncios). Choose currency and time zone carefully, because they are hard to change later. Check which payment methods work for your account from Mozambique.
Create the **Pixel** (Pixel da Meta) in Events Manager. Ask Lovable to add the Pixel base code to every page of your sales site.
Connect purchase tracking. Check whether EscalePay or Hotmart lets you add your Pixel ID to the checkout so that 'Purchase' events are sent. Then confirm with Meta's test events tool.
Create one campaign with the objective **Sales** (Vendas), one ad set and one daily budget.

blocks.text: **Advantage+** is Meta's automation. It decides who sees your ad and where (Feed, Reels, Stories), based on who actually buys. For a small test, keep targeting simple: Brazil, adults 18+, Portuguese. Then let the system find buyers. Don't stack 20 interests. Meta renames these options often, so check what Ads Manager shows today.

A prompt for Lovable: 'Add the Meta Pixel base code with ID [your ID] in the head section of every page, and fire a ViewContent event on the Caderno do Casal sales page.' Then open the page and check Events Manager. You should see the event within minutes.
Don't assume purchases are being tracked until you see a real test 'Purchase' event in Events Manager. Without it, Meta optimises blind and every number you read later is wrong.

sections.heading: The test plan

blocks.text: The plan from your playbook is R$20-30 per day, per product, for 5 to 7 days. That is about R$150-200 per test (around USD 30-40), plus about 12.15% Brazilian tax. Use 3 to 5 creatives (criativos, the videos or images in your ads), taken from your organic winners. Don't invent new ideas for ads. Use the posts that already proved people care.

blocks.title: Choosing creatives (example)
blocks.text: Say your best organic posts were: (A) a flip-through of the Caderno with 'Encontro 12: piquenique na sala' on screen, (B) a text-on-screen video '52 encontros = 1 por semana, o ano todo', and (C) a slideshow of 5 cards from the '100 Cartões de Perguntas para Casais' bump. These become ad creatives A, B and C. Re-edit each one in CapCut as 9:16 with a strong first 2 seconds and an end card showing the product name and price.

Don't touch the campaign every hour. Let it run at least 2-3 days before you judge anything. Big edits can reset Meta's learning, and you pay for that confusion. Write your decision rules **before** the test starts, while you are still calm.

sections.heading: Reading the numbers

blocks.title: Five numbers you must understand
items: **CTR (taxa de cliques):** clicks ÷ impressions. Does the creative make people stop and click?
**CPC (custo por clique):** spend ÷ clicks. How much each visitor costs.
**Cost per checkout (custo por início de checkout):** spend ÷ checkouts started. Does the page convince people?
**Cost per purchase (custo por compra):** spend ÷ purchases. The number that decides everything.
**ROAS (retorno sobre o gasto com anúncios):** revenue ÷ ad spend. A ROAS of 2 means R$2 came in for every R$1 spent, before fees and tax.

blocks.title: Worked example: 6-day test, R$50 per creative (fictional numbers)
What this table tells you
blocks.text: In total you spent R$150 and got 4 purchases, about R$132,40 in revenue before fees. The test as a whole lost money, which is normal for a first test. But Creative A cost R$16,67 per purchase. Add 12.15% tax and that's about R$18,69. Your AOV is R$33,10, and after the Hotmart-style fee you keep about R$27,33 per order. So A is profitable. Keep A, kill B and C, and put the whole R$25/day behind A.

Your playbook's rule is: scale only while cost per purchase is below your AOV. I add a safety line called **break-even (ponto de equilíbrio)**: what you keep per order after platform fees, divided by 1.1215 for the tax. In this example, R$27,33 ÷ 1.1215 = about **R$24 per purchase**. Below R$24, you profit. Between R$24 and R$33,10, you are close to zero. For reference only: Brazil's median CPM (cost per 1,000 impressions) is about USD 3.46 (range 1.77-7.45), and info-product CPC is around R$1-2,50. CPC data is inconsistent, though. Your own numbers are what matter.

sections.heading: Kill, keep, scale, and faceless creatives that work

blocks.title: My decision rules (write them in your sheet)
items: **Kill:** on decision day, any creative with zero purchases, or with cost per purchase above your AOV (R$33,10).
**Watch:** cost per purchase between break-even (about R$24) and AOV. Give it 2-3 more days or a new hook. Don't scale it.
**Keep:** cost per purchase below break-even.
**Early stop:** if after 3 days one creative is far worse than the others on CTR and CPC, turn it off and move its budget to the best one.
**Scale:** add 20-30% to the budget every 2-3 days, only while cost per purchase stays below AOV, and ideally below break-even.

blocks.title: Scaling a winner (example)
items: Day 0: R$25/day on Creative A.
Day 3: still below break-even? Raise to about R$31/day (+25%).
Day 6: still below break-even? Raise to about R$39/day.
Day 9: still below? About R$49/day. Above AOV? Go back to the last budget that worked.
Each time you scale, add one fresh creative made in the style of the winner, so you don't depend on a single ad.

blocks.text: Faceless creatives that suit your products: flip-throughs of the real pages, text-on-screen hooks, carousels of the inside pages, close-ups of hands writing in the planner, and slow B-roll of a table set for a date. Make Gemini art without text and add titles in Canva. Never show 'before/after' and never invent results.

sections.heading: Ad policies, taxes and protecting your cash

blocks.title: Policies you must respect
items: **No unrealistic outcomes or get-rich-quick claims:** no 'saia das dívidas em 30 dias', no 'renda extra garantida'. Brazilian law (CDC art. 37/67) and CONAR also ban misleading ads.
**No personal attributes:** don't say 'Você está endividado?' or 'Seu casamento está em crise?'. Describe the product instead: 'Planilha para organizar as contas de 2027'.
**Kids products are aimed at adults:** Kit Natal ads speak to teachers and parents. Never collect children's data.
**AI labels:** label realistic AI people or scenes. Meta also adds its own AI labels.
**Finance is educational only:** it is not investment advice. **Faith:** use Bible references and paraphrase, never verbatim NVI quotes.

blocks.title: Texto de anúncio honesto (Caderno do Casal)
blocks.text: Um encontro por semana, o ano inteiro. O Caderno do Casal traz 52 ideias de encontros para vocês fazerem juntos. [Descreva aqui o que tem dentro, só o que é verdade.] É um produto digital: você recebe por e-mail logo após a compra. R$27. Toque em 'Saiba mais' e veja as páginas por dentro.

**Taxes:** from 1 January 2026, Meta adds about 12.15% in Brazilian taxes to ad spend. A R$25 daily budget really costs about R$28,04, and a R$150 test costs about R$168,23. Check how the tax appears on your invoices as a foreign advertiser, and always put it inside your plan.

Set a daily budget **and** an account spending limit in Meta billing. Ad money comes only from profit or from money you can lose. Never borrow for ads. Never use a card you can't pay off this month. Never touch rent or food money. If a test fails, that's the price of a lesson, not a reason to 'win it back' with a bigger budget.
Ads should make your profit grow. Don't let them become a bill you're hoping to win back.

key_takeaways: Start ads only after organic sales prove the page converts, and only with money you can afford to lose.
Set up Business Manager, the Pixel and real Purchase tracking before you spend anything.
Test R$20-30/day per product for 5-7 days with 3-5 creatives taken from your organic winners.
Judge by cost per purchase against your AOV and your break-even, including the ~12.15% tax.
Kill losers on decision day. Scale winners by 20-30% every 2-3 days only while cost per purchase stays below AOV.
Respect Meta's policies: no unrealistic results, no personal attributes, kids' products aimed at adults, AI labels.

challenge.title: First test
challenge.mission: Set up Business Manager and the Pixel, prepare 3 creatives from your best organic posts, write your test plan and kill rules, and launch a R$20-30/day test only if Family 1 already has organic sales.
challenge.time_box: 2-3 days to set up, then 5-7 days of testing (only with the green light)
steps: Create your Business Manager, ad account, faceless brand Page and Instagram, and set an account spending limit.
Create the Pixel, add it to the Caderno do Casal page through Lovable, and confirm a test event in Events Manager. Check that your checkout can send Purchase events.
Pick the 3 best Family 1 organic posts by saves, shares, clicks or sales, and re-edit them as 9:16 ad creatives (art without text, titles in Canva, AI label where required).
Write the test plan in Google Sheets: product, daily budget (R$20-30), number of days (5-7), total including ~12.15% tax, AOV, break-even, kill/keep/scale rules and decision day.
Gate check: count Family 1's organic sales. Zero? Stop here and go back to content and affiliates. Some? Launch one Sales campaign aimed at Brazil, 18+.
Log spend, clicks, checkouts and purchases every morning, and make decisions only on decision day.
challenge.proof: A screenshot of Events Manager showing the Pixel receiving events, your test plan sheet, and, if launched, a screenshot of the campaign showing its budget and dates.
challenge.bonus: After the test, write a 5-line lesson: which hook won, cost per purchase against break-even, and what you will test next.

quiz.question: When should you start paid ads for a product?
options: On day 1, to get data fast
Only after organic sales show the page converts
When you can borrow money for a bigger budget
After 1,000 followers, even with zero sales
quiz.explanation: Ads multiply what already works. Without organic sales you don't know if the page converts, so ads would most likely just burn money.

quiz.question: A creative spent R$150 and brought 5 purchases. What is the cost per purchase?
quiz.explanation: R$150 ÷ 5 = R$30. That is below the R$33,10 AOV but above the example break-even of about R$24, so watch it and don't scale yet.

quiz.question: Which ad text is most likely to break Meta's personal attributes rule?
options: 'Planner para organizar 2027 mês a mês'
'Você está endividado?'
'52 ideias de encontros para casais'
'Kit de atividades de Natal para professores'
quiz.explanation: Asking about the viewer's personal situation (like debt) suggests you know their personal attributes. Describe the product instead.

glossary.meaning: Code on your page that tells Meta who viewed it, started checkout and bought.
The percentage of people who saw your ad and clicked it.
Ad spend divided by the number of clicks.
Ad spend divided by the number of purchases. The most important ad number.

glossary.pt: retorno sobre o gasto com anúncios
glossary.meaning: Revenue divided by ad spend.
The highest cost per purchase at which you neither win nor lose money.

chapters.title: Running the Empire
chapters.subtitle: Daily numbers, cash rules, the roadmap to Black Friday, and the 10-day launch
chapters.mentor_intro: Your products are live, content is running, affiliates are selling, and maybe you have a small ad test going. Now the game changes. The danger is no longer 'no sales'. The danger is chaos: money sitting in a platform you don't fully trust, refunds you didn't notice, ad spend that grew quietly, and a founder checking stats at 2 a.m. who burns out by December. In this chapter you become the CEO of a small, calm business. I give you a daily dashboard and a 20-minute morning routine, a weekly CEO review, and simple cash rules: withdraw often, keep separate accounts, and split your profit into taxes and reserve, reinvestment and your own pay. We cover formalising your business in Mozambique with an accountant, your product roadmap to Black Friday and beyond, when to hire your first freelancers, and how to protect your energy and your reputation. Then you face the final boss: the 10-day launch. Let's build something that lasts longer than one good week.
learning_goals: Run a daily dashboard and a 20-minute morning routine covering sales, AOV, refunds, ad spend and cash.
Hold a weekly CEO review that ends with clear decisions.
Manage cash with frequent withdrawals, separate accounts and a fixed profit split.
Prepare the right questions for an accountant about ISPC, VAT and currency rules.
Plan your roadmap from the 10-day launch to Black Friday and new language editions.

sections.heading: The daily dashboard and the 20-minute morning routine

blocks.text: A **dashboard (painel)** is one Google Sheet with one row per day. It's where the truth lives. Platforms show pretty charts. Your sheet shows what actually stayed with you.

blocks.title: The 20-minute morning routine
items: Minutes 0-5: open EscalePay and Hotmart and copy yesterday's sales, revenue and refunds into the sheet.
Minutes 5-9: answer support emails and refund requests. Honour the 7-day withdrawal right quickly and politely.
Minutes 9-13: check ads. Is spend inside your daily limit? Is cost per purchase below break-even? Apply your written rules, nothing else.
Minutes 13-16: check cash. If the platform balance is above your limit, withdraw today.
Minutes 16-20: choose today's 3 tasks: one for content, one for a product, one for affiliates.

blocks.title: One fictional morning
blocks.text: Yesterday: 14 orders, R$470,40 revenue, AOV R$33,60, 1 refund (reason: 'I thought it was printed and shipped'), ad spend R$25 + tax, platform balance R$380. Decisions: move the line 'produto digital, você recebe por e-mail' higher on the page, leave the ad running, and withdraw the balance today. Total time: 18 minutes.

Ask Claude to build the formulas: AOV = revenue ÷ orders; bump take rate = bump sales ÷ front sales; refund rate = refunds ÷ orders. Then check each formula against one example you calculated by hand before you trust it.

sections.heading: The weekly CEO review

blocks.text: Once a week, on the same day, give yourself 60 minutes as the CEO. You don't make content in this hour. You look at the whole week and make decisions.

blocks.title: Eight questions for every review
items: How many orders this week, and what was the AOV? Up or down?
Which product, bump and upsell sold best? Which one didn't sell at all?
Which content pieces and which affiliates brought the sales?
How many refunds, and why? Is the page promising something the product doesn't deliver?
Ads: total spend with tax, cost per purchase, kill/keep/scale decisions taken?
Cash: how much is still in platforms, and how much is safely in your account?
What is **one thing to double** and **one thing to stop** next week?
What are next week's 3 goals?

blocks.text: The review only counts if it ends with decisions written in your sheet. 'Interesting week' is not a decision. 'Stop the Pinterest board for Family 3, double the flip-through videos for Family 1' is. Your future self will thank you for writing it down.

sections.heading: Cash: withdraw, separate, split

blocks.text: EscalePay is your main checkout. But its international selling has **not** been independently verified: currencies, exchange spread, payout timing, holds and chargebacks (estornos) are unknown. So the rules are strict. Time your first payout. Withdraw often (every day once you have volume). Never keep big balances there. Hotmart pays foreign producers through Payoneer in USD, with about 2% on withdrawal and up to 2.75% on conversion according to third-party sources. Verify these fees when you sign up.

blocks.title: Profit split, my starting suggestion (adjust with your accountant)
Fictional month
blocks.text: Say you end a month with 20,000 MT profit after fees, ads and commissions. You move 6,000 MT to the taxes-and-reserve account, keep 6,000 MT for reinvestment, and pay yourself 8,000 MT. Keep three separate places: a business account, a reserve account and your personal account. Never mix business money with personal spending.

Currency rules in Mozambique can change. Banco de Moçambique's Aviso 1/GBM/2025 required 50% of export earnings to be converted. That rule was temporary and may end around October 2026, so check its current status now with your bank or accountant. Count the exchange spread as a real cost too.

sections.heading: Formalising: talk to an accountant

blocks.text: When sales become regular, you are running a business, not a hobby. Find an accountant (contabilista) in Mozambique and bring a written list of questions. Don't wait for 'big money'. Clean records from the first month are much easier than fixing a messy year later.

blocks.title: Questions to bring
items: Can I use **ISPC**, the simplified small-business tax? How do I register, and what does it cost me?
Does the reported **16% VAT on digital goods and services** apply to my sales to buyers in Brazil?
Is the Aviso 1/GBM/2025 export conversion rule still active? How should I receive USD and BRL payouts?
How should I show seller identification on my Brazilian pages (name, NUIT, contact) to meet **Decreto 7.962/2013** as a foreign seller?
Before I sell in EUR to Portugal: will I owe **EU VAT** from the first sale, or is my platform the merchant of record?
Which documents and records must I keep every month?

blocks.text: Everything in this section is 'check this'. Tax rules depend on your exact situation. Don't price in EUR or sell to Portugal until EU VAT is clear. Keep your LGPD privacy policy in Portuguese on every page, and get consent before sending marketing messages.

sections.heading: Your product roadmap

blocks.title: From the 10-day launch to new markets

blocks.text: **The bundle anchor must be honest.** The anchor price is the 'real value' figure shown next to the offer price. Your playbook lists the Mega Kit's anchor as R$207,60. When I add the nine full prices, I get R$207,70. Before you publish, add them again from your final price list and show the exact real sum. An anchor that is off by even 10 cents is still an anchor you can't defend.

blocks.title: Before the PT-PT and other editions
items: Portugal (~9.27M internet users) dislikes PT-BR, so rewrite the text properly. Don't just swap a few words. E-books sell at about EUR 7-47, and MB WAY/Multibanco make up ~80% of payments.
Angola (~17.6M internet users) has very restricted access to foreign currency and cards. Test payment before investing time.
Mozambique (~7.12M internet users): e-books sell at around 500 MT. Price for the local market.
Then a new product every 2 weeks, found with the Hotmart marketplace, TikTok search, Pinterest Trends, Google Trends and the Kiwify/Cakto top lists.

blocks.text: Use the same system for every new product: Claude drafts the content, sales copy and kit, Gemini makes art without text, Canva adds the titles, Lovable builds the page. You check every line. A system makes 'every 2 weeks' possible without losing quality.

sections.heading: Team, energy and reputation

blocks.text: Now the honest maths of 'sales every minute'. One sale per minute is 1,440 sales a day, about R$39k a day at R$27 (around USD 7k). That's top-product territory, which takes big ad budgets or huge affiliate armies. The real ladder is: first sale, then 10 a day, then 100 a day. 100 a day at R$27 plus bumps is about R$3,000 a day (~35,000 MT). Stories of 'a million in 15 days' usually show gross revenue before ad spend and refunds, or they are marketing for a course.

blocks.title: Your first team (later, paid from the reinvest bucket)
items: **Freelance designer or video editor** first, when making creatives takes most of your week.
**Virtual assistant (VA)** for support emails and affiliate questions, once replying daily stops you from creating.
Give each person a written step-by-step guide (Claude can draft it, you check it).
Never share your main passwords. Use team access roles where the platform offers them (check this).

blocks.text: Your energy is a business asset. Sleep 7-8 hours, work in fixed blocks, check your numbers in the morning and maybe once at night, and take one full day off each week. A burnt-out founder makes bad decisions about ads and money. I would rather see you calm at 10 sales a day than exhausted chasing 1,000.

blocks.title: Protecting your reputation
items: Reply to support within 24 hours and refund without arguing.
No fake testimonials, numbers, scarcity, rankings or before/after. Ever.
Remove affiliates who break the rules, quickly and quietly.
Label AI where required, keep finance content educational, and never collect children's data.

blocks.text: Hype might get you one big week. A calm system and a good reputation get you through the whole year.

key_takeaways: One daily dashboard and a 20-minute morning routine keep you in control of sales, AOV, refunds, ad spend and cash.
A weekly CEO review only counts if it ends with written decisions: one thing to double, one to stop, three goals.
Withdraw often, never keep big balances on unverified platforms, and split profit into taxes/reserve, reinvestment and your pay.
Formalise early: ask an accountant about ISPC, VAT, seller identification and currency rules before they become problems.
The roadmap: three families in 10 days, the Mega Kit for Black Friday 27-30 Nov 2026, then PT-PT, English and Spanish editions.
Scale honestly: first sale, then 10/day, then 100/day, while protecting your sleep and your reputation.
